extracted.intended_audience: general readers; students, scholars, and writers interested in Audre Lorde, feminist poetics, and intersectional literature
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles and evaluative criteria for producing poetry and prose informed by Audre Lorde's poetics and feminist theory — emphasizing technical skill, emotional honesty, intersectional subject matter, and language as resistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical mastery and emotional expression
rubrics_metrics.description: As a poet, she is well known for technical mastery and emotional expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lorde's work is noted for formal skill combined with powerful affect; strong poetry balances craft (meter, diction, form) with intense feeling and expressive force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressing anger and outrage about injustice
rubrics_metrics.description: Her poems ... express anger and outrage at civil and social injustices she observed throughout her life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetry that confronts systemic wrongs directly — harnessing righteous anger — is characteristic of Lorde's approach and can be an ethical and aesthetic stance in political writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry as naming the nameless
rubrics_metrics.description: "Poetry is the way we help give name to the nameless so it can be thought... As they become known to and accepted by us, our feelings and the honest exploration of them become sanctuaries and spawning grounds for the most radical and daring ideas."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good poetic practice includes using language to make previously unnamed experiences thinkable; intimate, candid self-exploration can generate novel, radical insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language as resistance / powerful spoken-word delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Lorde believed language was a powerful form of resistance; as a spoken word artist, her delivery has been called powerful, melodic, and intense by the Poetry Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In performance and written form, prioritize clarity, forceful diction, musicality, and emotional intensity; consider oral delivery as integral to a poem's power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multigenre and multicultural expression; resist categorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Her conception of her many layers of selfhood is replicated in the multi-genres of her work. Her refusal to be placed in a particular category ... was characteristic of her determination to come across as an individual rather than a stereotype.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow multiple genres, forms, and cultural influences to coexist in a single work; avoid forcing identity or text into narrow categories or stereotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bearing witness through personal prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Works like The Cancer Journals and A Burst of Light use non-fiction prose, including essays and journal entries, to bear witness to, explore, and reflect on ... diagnosis, treatment, recovery, and recurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memoir and essay can function as testimony: use candid, reflective prose to link personal experience to wider social/ethical questions; bearing witness should be both evocative and analytically clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use difference as a source of strength and creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: She emphasizes ... differences should not be used to divide; differences ... seen as a fund of necessary polarities between which our creativity can spark like a dialectic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than smoothing over differences, foreground them as productive tensions that generate insight and creative energy in writing and organizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersectionality / theory of difference
rubrics_metrics.description: Her writings are based on the 'theory of difference' ... She identified issues of race, class, age and ageism, sex and sexuality and, later ... chronic illness and disability; she argued that ... these other differences are also recognized and addressed. This theory is today known as intersectionality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective work should attend to multiple, intersecting axes of identity and oppression (race, gender, class, sexuality, disability, age), avoiding single-axis analysis or representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformation of silence into language and action
rubrics_metrics.description: In 'The Transformation of Silence into Language and Action', Lorde discusses the importance of speaking, even when afraid ... 'Your silence does not protect you.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for courageous self-disclosure in writing and speech; encourage moving from private fear to public articulation and activism — both ethically and rhetorically potent moves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject using the master's tools to dismantle oppression
rubrics_metrics.description: Her most famous essay, 'The Master's Tools Will Never Dismantle the Master's House', questions the scope and ability for change to be instigated when examining problems through a racist, patriarchal lens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique and avoid reproducing oppressive frameworks or methods in attempts to achieve liberation; interrogate whether strategies reproduce the very hierarchies they claim to oppose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibly use privilege; do not burden the marginalized with education
rubrics_metrics.description: People must educate themselves about the oppression of others because expecting a marginalized group to educate the oppressors is the continuation of racist, patriarchal thought. Privilege must be used to hold door open for other allies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers/activists with privilege should take responsibility for learning and amplify marginalized voices rather than expecting them to instruct or carry the emotional labor of educating others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reclaim the erotic as a source of power
rubrics_metrics.description: In 'The Erotic as Power' ... Lorde theorizes the Erotic as a site of power for women ... not only in reference to sexuality ... but also as a feeling of enjoyment, love, and thrill ... a source of power for women to live with passion in all areas of their life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the erotic broadly as an affective, creative source that can guide values and priorities in writing; resist its reduction to merely sexual or commodified meanings and foreground consent and mutual empowerment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty about pain and experience as political work
rubrics_metrics.description: She held that feelings are a form of self-knowledge that can inform and enrich activism; acknowledging and experiencing pain helps women to transcend it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuing emotional honesty in creative work: candid engagement with pain and vulnerability is both personally transformative and politically generative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical engagement with civil-rights and identity themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Her poems and prose largely deal with issues related to civil rights, feminism, lesbianism, illness, disability, and the exploration of Black female identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that engages explicitly with social justice, identity, illness, and marginalization topics aligns with Lorde's thematic commitments; meaningful engagement requires both lived insight and critical framing.
